author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Boeing and the Society of Professional Engineering Employees in Aerospace have reached a tentative four-year contract after union members overwhelmingly rejected an earlier offer in August. The revised proposal would provide a 10% general wage increase on October 16, followed by 4% annual increases plus merit raises through 2030.

The agreement also revises work-from-home rules and overtime limits. Union officials said members had pressed for larger across-the-board increases after Seattle-area inflation rose 4.5% over the previous year. SPEEA’s negotiating team said the package did not satisfy every demand but represented a meaningful improvement over Boeing’s prior proposal.

Members must still ratify the deal before the current contract expires on October 6. The vote matters beyond compensation: Boeing engineers are central to certification work for the delayed 737 MAX 10 and 777-9 aircraft. A rejection could revive the possibility of a strike at a time when both programs face schedule pressure. The tentative settlement is the first fully negotiated contract between the sides since 2012, after extensions in 2016 and 2020.
dek: The revised agreement would deliver a 10% initial raise and annual increases through 2030 as key certification programs remain delayed.
headline: Boeing engineers reach tentative four-year contract
